LESSON: TAWBAH

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Devotional Acts
Topic 4.2: Tawbah

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Tawbah. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should a Muslim seek repentance from Allah (S.W.T.)?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. state the conditions of tawbah as a basis for forgiveness from Allah (S.W.T.)
2. practise actions that lead to tawbah as a way of purifying one from sins
3. appreciate the virtue of tawbah as a condition for success in this life and the Hereafter

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: TAWBAH
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Tawbah helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: TAWBAH
Study Tawbah like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: State the conditions of tawbah as a basis for forgiveness from Allah (S.W.T.)

What this means
In this part you learn to state the conditions of tawbah as a basis for forgiveness from Allah (S.W.T.). You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: state the conditions of tawbah as a basis for forgiveness from Allah (S.W.T.).
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Tawbah” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can state the conditions of tawbah as a basis for forgiveness from Allah (S.W.T.). Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Practise actions that lead to tawbah as a way of purifying one from sins

What this means
In this part you learn to practise actions that lead to tawbah as a way of purifying one from sins. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise actions that lead to tawbah as a way of purifying one from sins.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Tawbah in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise actions that lead to tawbah as a way of purifying one from sins. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the virtue of tawbah as a condition for success in this life and the Hereafter

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the virtue of tawbah as a condition for success in this life and the Hereafter. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the virtue of tawbah as a condition for success in this life and the Hereafter.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the virtue of tawbah as a condition for success in this life and the Hereafter. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Tawbah is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Tawbah” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: state the conditions of tawbah as a basis for forgiveness from Allah (S.W.T.))

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Tawbah in your own words. (skill: practise actions that lead to tawbah as a way of purifying one from sins)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate the virtue of tawbah as a condition for success in this life and the Hereafter)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Tawbah to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: state the conditions of tawbah as a basis for forgiveness from Allah (S.W.T.).
3. Practise this skill: practise actions that lead to tawbah as a way of purifying one from sins.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the virtue of tawbah as a condition for success in this life and the Hereafter.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Tawbah from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Tawbah: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Tawbah?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should a Muslim seek repentance from Allah (S.W.T.)?
2. How should Muslims seek repentance from Allah (S.W.T.)?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Tawbah means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: state the conditions of tawbah as a basis for forgiveness from Allah (S.W.T.).
5. Be able to: practise actions that lead to tawbah as a way of purifying one from sins.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
